341220.title: The asymptotic conjecture for minimum splitters of splittable set families
341220.statement:
Let a **splittable $n$-set family** be a family of $n$ sets admitting at least one splitter, and let $k$ denote the size of the underlying ground set. **The asymptotic splitter conjecture.** The minimum number of splitters of a splittable $n$-set family is asymptotic to

$$
\frac{2^k}{k^{n/2}}.
$$

The cases $n=1$ and $n=2$ are known, and computational evidence supports the $n=3$ case; the general assertion remains open.
341220.source_name: Samuel Coskey, Bryce Frederickson, Samuel Mathers and Hao-Tong Yan, “On splitting and splittable families”, arXiv:1811.12896 (2022).
341220.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.12896

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2018).

341979.title: Superlinear area conjecture for subtree-separated orthogonal drawings of complete ternary trees
341979.statement:
Let $T$ be an $n$-node complete ternary tree. A planar straight-line orthogonal drawing of $T$ has the **subtree separation property** if the drawings of the subtrees rooted at distinct children of every node are separated as specified in the paper. Area is the area of the smallest axis-parallel enclosing rectangle of the drawing.

**Superlinear area conjecture.** There exists a constant $\varepsilon>0$ such that every $n$-node complete ternary tree requires

$$
\Omega(n^{1+\varepsilon})
$$

area in any planar straight-line orthogonal drawing satisfying the subtree separation property.

The conjecture is motivated by computational experiments on complete ternary trees and concerns a restricted class of drawings. The unrestricted asymptotic area requirements for ternary trees, and for complete ternary trees, remain open in the source.
341979.source_name: Barbara Covella, Fabrizio Frati and Maurizio Patrignani, “On the Area Requirements of Planar Straight-Line Orthogonal Drawings of Ternary Trees”, arXiv:1902.11044 (2019).
341979.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.11044

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2019).

343305.title: Asymptotic equivalence conjecture for powerful 132-avoidance
343305.statement:
Let $\Omega_n^T(\tau)$ be the set of permutations in $S_n$ whose powers indexed by $T$ avoid $\tau$, and let $\operatorname{PAv}_n(132)$ and $\operatorname{SAv}_n(132)$ denote the sets of permutations that powerfully and strongly avoid $132$, respectively.

**Powerful 132-avoidance asymptotic conjecture.** As $n$ tends to infinity,

$$
\left|\Omega_n^{\{1,2,3\}}(132)\right|\sim\left|\operatorname{PAv}_n(132)\right|\sim\left|\operatorname{SAv}_{n-1}(132)\right|.
$$

The conjecture is based on numerical evidence. The source explicitly says that none of the three implied asymptotic equivalences is known.
343305.source_name: Amanda Burcroff and Colin Defant, “Pattern-Avoiding Permutation Powers”, arXiv:1907.09451 (2020).
343305.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.09451

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

345545.title: The growth constant for the stack-sorting map
345545.statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, let $s:S_n\to S_n$ be the stack-sorting map, and let $\deg(s:S_n\to S_n)$ denote its maximum fiber size. The paper considers the exponential growth rate

$$
\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\deg(s:S_n\to S_n)^{1/n}.
$$

**Stack-sorting growth conjecture.** The value of this limit lies in the interval $(1.68,1.73)$.

The interval is suggested by computations on random permutations for $n=100$ and $n=300$. The problem of obtaining improved asymptotic estimates, or exact formulas, remains open.
345545.source_name: Colin Defant and James Propp, “Quantifying Noninvertibility in Discrete Dynamical Systems”, arXiv:2002.07144 (2020).
345545.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.07144

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2020).

347590.title: Conjecture on the asymptotic threshold for asymmetric choosability
347590.statement:
For positive integers $k_A$ and $k_B$, let $\xi_m(k_A)$ denote the asymptotic threshold parameter for the choosability of complete bipartite graphs, and let $\xi_g(k_A)$ be a positive constant. A bipartite graph is $(k_A,k_B)$-choosable when every list assignment with list sizes $k_A$ and $k_B$ on the two parts admits a proper coloring.

**Asymptotic threshold conjecture.** There exist positive constants $\xi_g(k_A)$ such that every bipartite graph $G$ satisfying $\xi<\xi_g(k_A)$ is $(k_A,k_B)$-choosable. Moreover, if the $\xi_g(k_A)$ are chosen to be the largest constants for which this statement is true, then

$$
\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\log(\xi_g(k_A))}{k_A}
$$

exists.

The source says that this conjecture implies all three parts of the asymmetric Alon–Cambie–Kang conjecture. The notation and the precise definition of $\xi$ are not included in the supplied context, so the formulation and status should be checked against the paper.
347590.source_name: Daniel G. Zhu, “Coloring bipartite graphs with semi-small list size”, arXiv:2008.06040 (2023).
347590.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.06040

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

348108.title: The limiting energy conjecture for Barabási–Albert trees
348108.statement:
Let $\{X_n\}_{n>0}$ be a sequence of trees with parameter $\alpha$, and let $\mathcal{E}(X_n)$ denote the graph energy of $X_n$.

**Limiting energy conjecture.** For every $\alpha$, there exists $g(\alpha)$ such that, almost surely,

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\mathcal{E}(X_n)}{n}=g(\alpha).
$$

Moreover, $g(\alpha)>1$ for $\alpha<0.79$, $g(\alpha)<1$ for $\alpha>0.81$, $g(\alpha)$ is strictly decreasing and continuous in $\alpha$, $g(\alpha)\to0$ as $\alpha\to\infty$, and $g(\alpha)\to1.273$ as $\alpha\to\infty$.

These claims formalize simulation observations about the asymptotic energy density of the random trees. In particular, the claim at $\alpha=0$ would imply that random recursive random trees are not hypoenergetic. The final two limiting assertions are internally inconsistent as written, since both use $\alpha\to\infty$; the source should be checked for a likely typographical error.
348108.source_name: Octavio Arizmendi and Emilio Dominguez, “Barabasi-Albert trees are hypoenergetic”, arXiv:2009.13784 (2020).
348108.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.13784

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2020).

352307.title: Central moment conjecture for continuously increasing subsequences
352307.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{S}_{m,n}$ be the set of multiset permutations under consideration, let $\pi$ be uniformly random in $\mathfrak{S}_{m,n}$, and let $L^1_{m,n}(\pi)$ be the continuously increasing subsequence statistic. Define

$$
\mu=\mathbb{E}[L^1_{m,n}(\pi)].
$$

For each $r\ge 1$, define

$$
c_r=\begin{cases}\dfrac{r!}{2^{r/2}(r/2)!}& r\text{ even},\\[4pt]\dfrac{r!}{3\cdot 2^{(r-1)/2}((r-3)/2)!}& r\text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

**Central moment conjecture.** For all $r\ge 1$, if $n$ is sufficiently large in terms of $m$, then

$$
\mathbb{E}[(L^1_{m,n}(\pi)-\mu)^r]=c_r m^{\left\lfloor r/2\right\rfloor}+O\left(m^{\left\lfloor r/2\right\rfloor-1}\right).
$$

The conjecture is based on computational evidence for higher moments. Together with the known asymptotic standard deviation $\sigma\sim m^{1/2}$, it would imply convergence of the standardized moments to the Gaussian moments, and hence convergence in distribution to a standard normal law.
352307.source_name: Alexander Clifton, Bishal Deb, Yifeng Huang, Sam Spiro and Semin Yoo, “Continuously Increasing Subsequences of Random Multiset Permutations”, arXiv:2110.10315 (2021).
352307.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.10315

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

352805.title: Asymptotic enumeration conjecture for integer tetrahedra by perimeter
352805.statement:
Let $\tn$ denote the number of integer tetrahedra of perimeter $n$, counted up to congruence. **Asymptotic enumeration conjecture.** The number $\tn$ satisfies

$$
\tn \sim \frac{n^5}{229024} \qquad \text{as } n\to\infty.
$$

This conjecture is motivated by computational data suggesting a power-law growth of degree five, but the numerical value of the denominator remains uncertain.
352805.source_name: James East, Michael Hendriksen and Laurence Park, “On the enumeration of integer tetrahedra”, arXiv:2112.00899 (2021).
352805.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.00899

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2021).

358020.title: Asymptotic formula for linear-system chromatic number
358020.statement:
For integers $k\ge 3$, let $f_1(e,q,k)$ denote the maximum chromatic number of a $1$-$(q,k)$-system with $e$ $q$-cliques. **The asymptotic chromatic-number conjecture.** Fix $k\ge 3$. There exists $C=C_k>0$ such that if $e>q^C$, then

$$
f_1(e,q,k)=\Theta\!\left(e^{\frac{1}{2k-2}}q\right)\qquad(q\to\infty).
$$

The conjecture predicts the sharp order of magnitude in the large-$e$ regime, improving the preceding upper and lower bounds. The source describes the problem as wide open for smaller values of $e$ and gives no resolution of this asserted asymptotic statement.
358020.source_name: Dhruv Mubayi and Jacques Verstraete, “Coloring hypergraphs that are the union of nearly disjoint cliques”, arXiv:2304.04855 (2023).
358020.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.04855

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2023). “Classical old open questions in projective geometry ask for the maximum size of caps in various projective spaces.”

358865.title: The density conjecture for distance-restricted firefighting on square grids
358865.statement:
Let $P_n$ be the path graph on $n$ vertices, let $P_n\mathbin{\square}P_n$ be the Cartesian-product square grid, and let $\operatorname{DRMVS}(G,s;d,b)$ denote the maximum number of vertices saved in the distance-restricted firefighting process on graph $G$, starting from source $s$, with distance restriction $d$ and $b$ firefighter available per time step. The fire starts at the central vertex $((\lceil n/2\rceil,\lceil n/2\rceil))$ of the square grid, with one firefighter and distance restriction one. **The density conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{\operatorname{DRMVS}\left(P_n \mathbin{\square} P_n,\left(\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil,\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil\right);1,1\right)}{n^2} = \frac18
$$

This conjectures the asymptotic proportion of vertices saved in the one-firefighter, distance-one process on increasingly large square grids. The supplied text reports computational evidence from many square-grid instances but gives no proof or resolution.
358865.source_name: Andrea C. Burgess, John Hawkin, Alexander Howse, John Marcoux and David A. Pike, “Distance-Restricted Firefighting on Finite Graphs”, arXiv:2306.12575 (2025).
358865.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.12575

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2023).

364593.title: The alternating-group derangement bound conjecture
364593.statement:
Let $G=A_n$ be a finite simple transitive permutation group with point stabiliser $H$, and let $\delta(G)$ denote the proportion of derangements in the action.

**Alternating-group derangement bound conjecture.** The following hold:

$$
\delta(G)\geqslant\frac{13}{45},
$$

with equality if and only if $G=A_8$ and $H={\rm AGL}_3(2)$; and, if $n\geqslant9$,

$$
\delta(G)\geqslant\frac{[n!/e]}{n!}-\frac{(-1)^n(n-1)}{n!},
$$

with equality if and only if $H=A_{n-1}$.

The second assertion gives the proposed non-asymptotic formula for the natural action and would make $13/45$ the optimal lower-bound constant for alternating groups. The source presents these statements as a conjecture based on computations.
364593.source_name: Timothy C. Burness and Marco Fusari, “On derangements in simple permutation groups”, arXiv:2409.01043 (2025).
364593.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.01043

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2024).

365487.title: Thouless-type spectral-measure inequality for the critical almost Mathieu operator
365487.statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be coprime integers with $q$ odd, and let $\Sigma_{p/q}$ denote the periodic almost Mathieu spectrum. Let $C=0.915\ldots$ be Catalan's constant. **Thouless-type spectral-measure conjecture.** For $p\ne1,q-1$,

$$
\frac{32C}{\pi}>q\cdot|\Sigma_{p/q}|>q\cdot|\Sigma_{1/q}|>\sqrt{\frac{2}{q}}.
$$

The inequalities refine the known asymptotic relation between the measure of rational-frequency spectra and rational approximation to an irrational frequency. They were verified computationally for $q\le95$, but are not established in general.
365487.source_name: Jordi-Lluís Figueras and Joaquim Puig, “Computer Validation of Open Gaps for the Almost Mathieu Operator with Critical Coupling”, arXiv:2410.18536 (2025).
365487.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.18536

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

366896.title: Thomas's cubic-graph monophonic position conjecture
366896.statement:
Let $G$ be a cubic graph of order $n$, and let $\operatorname{mp}(G)$ denote its monophonic position number. **Thomas's conjecture.** The largest possible monophonic position number of a cubic graph with order $n$ is

$$
\frac{n}{3}+O(n).
$$

This conjecture was suggested by computational results; the stated asymptotic form remains unresolved in the survey.
366896.source_name: Ullas Chandran S. V., Sandi Klavžar and James Tuite, “The General Position Problem: A Survey”, arXiv:2501.19385 (2026).
366896.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19385

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2025). “Another open problem is given in the following conjectured Nordhaus-Gaddum relation.”

368881.title: McDonald–Sahay–Wyman's conjecture on the VC-dimension of Paley graphs
368881.statement:
Let $N$ be prime, and let $b[?2004l\Gamma=\Gamma(N)$ be the Paley (di)graph on $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$. The **VC-dimension** $\operatorname{VCdim}(\Gamma)$ is the maximum cardinality of a set shattered by the neighborhoods of $\Gamma$.

**McDonald–Sahay–Wyman's conjecture.** As $N\to\infty$ through the primes,

$$
\operatorname{VCdim}(\Gamma)=(1+o(1))\log_2 N.
$$

This conjecture is motivated by the analogous asymptotic behavior of random Cayley graphs and by the pseudorandomness of Paley graphs. The source mentions partial progress and numerical evidence, but does not state a resolution.
368881.source_name: Brad Rodgers and Anurag Sahay, “The VC-dimension of random subsets of finite groups”, arXiv:2506.14219 (2025).
368881.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.14219

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2025).

372765.title: Asymptotic conjecture for near-perfect powers of overpartition numbers
372765.statement:
Let $\overline{p}(n)$ denote the overpartition function, and define $M_{\overline{p},k}(d)$ analogously to $M_k(d)$ as the largest index whose overpartition number lies within $d$ of a $k$th power. **The overpartition asymptotic conjecture.** For $k\geq 2$,

$$
M_{\overline{p},k}(d)\sim\frac{1}{\pi^2}\left(\frac{k}{k-1}\right)^2(\log d)^2
$$

as $d\to\infty$. This is motivated by computational data and remains unproved.
372765.source_name: Summer Haag, Praneel Samanta, Swati, Holly Swisher, Stephanie Treneer and Robin Visser, “Repellent properties of perfect powers on partition functions: a heuristic approach”, arXiv:2601.18138 (2026).
372765.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18138

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2026). “This conjecture has been verified for all $n \leq 10^8$ by Alekseyev , but still remains an open problem.”

373432.title: Kotesovic's asymptotic conjecture for the number of Matryoshkas
373432.statement:
Let $m_n$ be the number of maximal Matryoshkas on an $(n+2)$-gon, with $m_1=1$ and

$$
m_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(k+1)m_km_{n-k}\quad\text{for }n\geq 2.
$$
 **Kotesovic's asymptotic conjecture.** The number of Matryoshkas satisfies

$$
m_n\sim c\cdot n!\cdot n^4,
$$

where $c=0.005428\ldots$. The conjecture is based on numerical evidence and concerns asymptotics of a simple $D$-algebraic generating series; the source gives no proof or resolution.
373432.source_name: Federico Ardila-Mantilla, Nima Arkani-Hamed, Carolina Figueiredo and Francisco Vazão, “Combinatorics of the Cosmohedron”, arXiv:2603.03425 (2026).
373432.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03425

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).

373488.title: Conjectural description of maximizers for the maximum product of distances
373488.statement:
Let $n\ge 3$. Let $P=\\{z_1,\dots,z_n\\}\subset\mathbb{C}$ be an $n$-gon with $\operatorname{diam}(P)\le 2$ that attains $\Delta(P)=\Delta_{\max}(n)$. 

**Maximizer structure conjecture.** The following properties hold:

1. If $n$ is odd, $P$ is a regular $n$-gon.
2. If $n$ is even, $P$ has an axis of symmetry. Moreover, if $6\mid n$, then $P$ is invariant under rotation by $2\pi/3$, and hence has dihedral symmetry compatible with this $120^\circ$ rotational symmetry.
3. If $n$ is even, the diameter graph of $P$ is obtained from a cycle $C_{n-3}$ by attaching three pendant edges to vertices of the cycle.

This conjecture refines the structural restrictions and numerical evidence developed in the paper, including the observed behavior for small $n$ and explicit asymptotic constructions. The proposed description remains conjectural because the extremal configurations for finite $n$ are difficult to determine; proving these properties would give a substantially sharper characterization of the maximizers.
373488.source_name: Stijn Cambie, Arne Decadt, Yanni Dong, Tao Hu and Quanyu Tang, “On the maximum product of distances of diameter 2 point sets”, arXiv:2603.07088 (2026).
373488.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.07088

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).

373769.title: Conway–Guttman asymptotics conjecture for occurrences of length-four patterns
373769.statement:
Let $S_{n,r}(q)$ denote the set of permutations of length $n$ with $r$ copies of the pattern $q$, and let $S_n(q)$ denote the set of permutations of length $n$ avoiding $q$. For a pattern $q$, write $|S_{n,r}(q)|$ and $|S_n(q)|$ for their cardinalities.

**Conway–Guttman conjecture.** For $q
\in \{4321,4312\}$, there is a constant $K$ such that

$$
|S_{n,r}(q)| \sim K|S_n(q)|.
$$

For $q\in \{4123,3412,4231,4213,3142\}$, there is a constant $K$ such that

$$
|S_{n,r}(q)| \sim Kn^r|S_n(q)|.
$$

This conjecture concerns the seven effective Wilf classes of patterns of length four and is supported by substantial numerical evidence. The paper proves asymptotic results for some of these patterns, but the stated general asymptotics remain conjectural.
373769.source_name: Michael Waite, “Permutations with a fixed number of occurrences of a pattern: A case generalizing 231”, arXiv:2603.21625 (2026).
373769.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21625

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).

382036.title: Minimal-size conjecture for tight irreducible affine vector space partitions
382036.statement:
An **affine vector space partition** is a partition into affine subspaces. It is **tight** if the intersection of the linear parts of all its pieces contains only the zero vector, and **irreducible** if no proper subset of more than one part has a union that is a part. The size of a partition is its number of parts.

**Affine-vector-space minimal-size conjecture.** The minimal size of a tight irreducible affine vector space partition of length $n$ is

$$
\frac{3}{2}n-o(n).
$$

Computations in the paper give minimal sizes $4,6,7,8,10$ for lengths $3,4,5,6,7$, respectively. The stated asymptotic behavior is suggested by later constructions but remains open.
382036.source_name: Yuval Filmus, Edward Hirsch, Sascha Kurz, Ferdinand Ihringer, Artur Riazanov, Alexander Smal and Marc Vinyals, “Irreducible subcube partitions”, arXiv:2212.14685 (2023).
382036.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.14685

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).

382109.title: Asymptotic separation between systolic bounds for Ramanujan surfaces
382109.statement:
Let $g$ denote the genus of a hyperbolic surface, let $\sys(M)$ denote its systole, and let $\Nsmall$ and $\lambda_1(M)$ be the quantities used in the paper. The first quantity below is the smallest upper bound on the systole obtainable from Theorem 3.1, and the second is the smallest lower bound on the systole sufficient to prove $\Nsmall<2$, equivalently $\lambda_1(M)>1/4$, using Theorem 3.2. **Asymptotic systolic-gap conjecture.** There exist constants $c_1>c_2$ such that these two bounds are respectively of the form

$$
2\log(g)+c_j+o(1)\quad\text{as}\quad g\to\infty.
$$

The conjecture predicts an asymptotic gap between the systolic upper bound and the lower bound required by the paper's method to establish the Ramanujan property. The source presents this as a conjecture motivated by numerical experiments and asymptotic results; no resolution is given.
382109.source_name: Maxime Fortier Bourque and Bram Petri, “Linear programming bounds for hyperbolic surfaces”, arXiv:2302.02540 (2026).
382109.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.02540

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2023).
